big_idea: We collect data by asking and counting. Tally marks group by FIVES so we can count fast.
learning_intention: We are learning to collect data and record it with tally marks.
student_learning_goal: I can collect data and record it with tally marks.
success_criteria: I can ask a survey question.
I can draw 4 vertical tallies and a 5th cross.
I can total my tallies by 5s.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Detective Dot and Tally puppets — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Lesson 2 tally tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Tally: Who likes APPLES? Hands up! Now let's count with TALLY MARKS — one line per hand!
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Detective Dot + Tally puppets. 'Friends — yesterday we sorted. Today we COLLECT DATA with TALLY MARKS.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write TALLY on chart. 'Tally = a line we draw to count one thing. We group by 5.'

Demonstrate the rule. Draw on chart: | || ||| |||| then on the FIFTH count, draw a CROSS ✗ through the four. '1, 2, 3, 4, FIVE — cross over!' Now |||| (with cross) is a group of 5.

More: ||||・|||| = 5 + 4 = 9. ||||・||||・||| = 5 + 5 + 3 = 13.

Now practice with the class. 'Who likes APPLES? Hands up.' Count and tally as children raise hands. 'Bea raised her hand. |. Finn raised. ||. Coco raised. |||. Maple raised. ||||. Dee raised. ||||CROSS — that's 5!'

More questions:
- 'Who has a pet at home?' Tally as hands raise.
- 'Who walked to school today?' Tally.
- 'Who likes hockey?' Tally.

'Tally says — count by 5s. We can total fast: 5, 10, 15, 20!'

'Today YOU survey classmates and tally results.'
student_actions: Listen to Tally count the class.

steps.instruction: Whole group: tally 4 class surveys. (a) likes apples. (b) has a pet. (c) walked to school. (d) likes hockey.

Three stations. Station A: Pick a Survey Card and tally answers from 5 classmates. Station B: Total Tallies — practice adding tally totals (||||CROSS + |||| = ?). Station C: Make a Question — pair invents their own survey question and tallies.
Stretch challenge at Station C: tally 10 classmates and total.
Discuss the cross-out rule. 'After the 4th, the 5th CROSSES. Now you have a group of 5 you can count fast.'
steps.teacher_prompt: Demonstrate counting by 5s using tally groups.

steps.instruction: Circulate to record formative evidence on the tally tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Ask 'How many tallies? Total?' Mark the tracker.

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Just survey 3 classmates.
differentiation.for_extending: Stretch at Station C: 10+ surveys, then total by 5s.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide a tally template with 1-2-3-4-CROSS already drawn as model.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children physically line up by their answer; teacher tallies the lines.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: asks survey question; draws correct 4+1 tally; totals tallies by 5s.

consolidation.exit_routine: Each child draws ONE tally total: '___ tallies = ___'.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 2 captures D1.2 mastery for survey collection and tallying.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child draws 5 vertical lines for 5 — repairing the no-cross trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-1 trap on D1.2 is the no-cross trap: the child draws 5 separate vertical lines for 5 instead of using the 4+1 cross convention. They miss that the cross is what makes counting BY FIVES fast.

This matters because tallies must be readable at a glance. A row of 47 vertical lines is countable but slow; the same 47 in 9 cross groups is countable in 5 seconds.

The walkthrough covers when a child draws all-vertical tallies.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. Child surveys 7 classmates. Draws 7 vertical lines: |||||||. Says 'I tallied 7'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You drew 7. But Tally says — every 5th tally, we CROSS through the four.'

Draw alongside. 'Look — 1, 2, 3, 4 are vertical. The 5th goes ACROSS like this ✗. Now I have ||||CROSS = 5. Then I keep going: 6, 7 are vertical again.'

Walk through. 'See — when I count, I say "5! And 2 more = 7". Fast!'

Generalise. 'Detective Dot says — group by 5. The cross is the secret. It lets us count BIG numbers fast.'

Now practice. Ask child to redraw 7 with the rule. Then 13 (||||CROSS ||||CROSS |||).

If still all-vertical: provide a stamping template with 4+1 marks pre-drawn. Force the cross.

Long-term recovery: every tally activity uses 4+1 cross convention.
expected_student_responses: (Mid) Crosses with prompts; shaky after the first 5.
(Strong) Crosses every 5th independently; counts by 5s aloud.
(Stretched) Knows the total by skip-counting (5, 10, 15) before recounting individuals.
common_misconceptions: 5 = 5 vertical lines. (Repair: use the 4+1 cross convention.)
Tallies are just counting. (Repair: tally + cross is GROUP COUNTING.)
Cross at any time. (Repair: cross only on the 5th of a group.)
recovery_moves: Use a tally template with model groups.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Independent practice of D1.2 tally collection.

parts_outline.task: Read 5 tally totals. Write the number each one shows.
Survey 5 classmates. Pick a question. Tally their answers.
Make your own tally chart. Survey 8 classmates. Total each row.
